outcomeDiff: No difference — expected and actual match (96 assertions, exit 0, validate green).
limitations: MVP S1 only: this is a library seam (pure plan/run/aggregate + injected runLens), not an end-to-end review CLI. The real review agent, per-finding adversarial verification + finding_add ledger mapping (S2), the completeness critic (S3), and the round/reopen escalation loop (S4) are deliberately out of scope and build on this surface. The §4.2 crash-safety/edge->lattice-review-behavior choice is one of the two spec-permitted lanes (the other is -quality).
pitfalls: Dual-host adversarial review (Codex host-2 + 5 Claude lanes + a 9-agent multi-lens Workflow) caught real test-strength gaps the first smoke missed: the dedup test passed the same LensDef object twice (could not distinguish lensId-dedup from object-identity-dedup) and the no-dedup test used differing findings (a content-deduping impl would still pass) — both Codex MAJOR; the 1-finding collectRawFindings flatten was never actually called (test-coverage HIGH); raw .find()! would crash instead of a named FAIL (quality MED); two mutation-reasoning intents were only reasoned not asserted. Round 2 hardened the smoke 65->96 assertions and rewrote 4 over-claiming evidence notes honest. The module code itself was correct throughout — all defects were in test strength + evidence honesty. Codex exec hung twice on stdin when backgrounded; fix is to redirect stdin from /dev/null (exec then completes fast). Next person: run codex host-2 with </dev/null.
